title: RemoteCheckResult
description:
Answer of `POST /v1/diagnostics/remote-check`: one check per distinct endpoint and scheme of
the primary remotes of the index, sorted by scheme, then endpoint.

endpoint.description:
The endpoint: `user@host[:port]` for SSH (an SSH alias as written), `scheme://host[:port]`
for HTTP(S) and `git://`, the URL of a local or other remote.

remote.description: Name of that repository's primary remote.

via.description: Slug of the repository the check ran in.

RemoteCheckOutcome.description: Result of `git ls-remote` against one remote.

oneOf.description: git failed, timed out or could not start.

error.description: What went wrong: exit status, timeout, or why git could not start.

problem.description: What kind of failure, from git's error output.

stderr_tail.description: The end of git's standard error, at most 2,000 bytes.

RemoteProblem.description: Why git could not reach a remote, read from its error output.

oneOf.description: SSH refused the key, or the host key is unknown.
HTTP(S) authentication failed, or git has no credential and cannot prompt.
The remote answered that the repository does not exist (moved, deleted, access lost).
The host could not be reached: name resolution, connection, timeout.

RemoteScheme.description: Transport of a remote, as `POST /v1/diagnostics/remote-check` groups remotes.

oneOf.description: A local path or a `file://` URL.
Any other transport (`ext::`, a remote helper…).
